## (b) Decision heuristics (D1-D6)

**D1 – what to test next**
- Set up situations where the model is tempted toward baby versions of the scary behaviours. 
  > "I’m excited for people working on “scary demos”, where we try to set up situations where our models exhibit tendencies which are the baby versions of the scary power-seeking/deceptive behaviors that we’re worried will lead to AI catastrophe."  
  > -- `research__the_case_for_becoming_a_black_box_investigator_of__3d5d3a1f` (2022-05-06; solo author) 
  > "“have humans try to get to know the AIs really well by observing their behaviors, so that they’re able to come up with inputs where the AIs will be tempted to do bad things, so that we can do adversarial training” is probably worth including in the smorgasbord of techniques"  
  > -- `research__the_case_for_becoming_a_black_box_investigator_of__3d5d3a1f` (2022-05-06; solo author)
- Test the axis along which the model can tell the deployment context from fakes. 
  > "the model decides that it’s only going to take dangerous actions on inputs that it’s convinced couldn’t have been synthetically generated."  
  > -- `research__behavioral_red_teaming_is_unlikely_to_produce_clea_ff0a83d6` (2024-10-10; solo author) 
  > "Some safety measures are implicitly visible to them (e.g. if we use techniques that sometimes replace their actions with the actions of a different model, they’ll probably notice this)."  
  > -- `research__thoughts_on_the_conservative_assumptions_in_ai_con_79585e0f` (2025-01-17; solo author)
- Pick settings close to the real concern (software engineering, AI R&D), with multi-service stateful environments rather than simple ones. 
  > "Because my main concern is AIs misusing their access to compute and proprietary models while doing ML R&D, I'm most interested in settings where the AIs are doing software engineering or using computers for tasks similar to those done by researchers in AI companies."  
  > -- `research__why_it_s_hard_to_make_settings_for_high_stakes_con_ff38a639` (2025-07-18; solo author) 
  > "a setting that is too simple may make sabotage easy to detect for reasons that do not transfer to deployment, while a setting with too little task diversity may yield narrow or noisy conclusions."  
  > -- `research__linuxarena_a_control_setting_for_ai_agentsin_live__48e03bb2` (2026-04-16; middle author)
- Hold out part of the environments to reduce contamination. 
  > "We release 10 of the 20 environments publicly and withhold the remaining 10 to reduce the risk of training data contamination."  
  > -- `research__linuxarena_a_control_setting_for_ai_agentsin_live__48e03bb2` (2026-04-16; middle author)

**D2 – what to collect**
- Replay the exact real input strings instead of writing fake continuations. 
  > "whatever input you'd given to the AI before you sampled a previous action, that's just some string that you can produce by the same process that you produced it the first time. So there's actually no difficulty going back in time here."  
  > -- `research__214_buck_shlegeris_on_controlling_ai_that_wants_to_57e8f430` (2025-04-04; solo author) 
  > "Instead of just producing synthetic attacks upfront, you can construct synthetic attacks by taking real contexts and modifying them minimally to contain attacks, and rerun this process regularly throughout deployment."  
  > -- `research__how_to_prevent_collusion_when_using_untrusted_mode_07a37f70` (2024-09-25; solo author)
- Reduce or paraphrase context to leave fewer tells. 
  > "If you can reduce the amount of context the monitor sees, it's less likely to notice tells that allow it to realize that the input was fake."  
  > -- `research__how_to_prevent_collusion_when_using_untrusted_mode_07a37f70` (2024-09-25; solo author)
- Keep model-attributed text something the model would plausibly have written. 
  > "models might naturally be able to notice when words have been “put in their mouth”--that is, when a context contains text that they supposedly generated, but that they actually would be very unlikely to generate."  
  > -- `research__how_to_prevent_collusion_when_using_untrusted_mode_07a37f70` (2024-09-25; solo author)
- Strip task purpose and domain to prevent selective behaviour. 
  > "If you're able to give them questions while disguising what domain the question was from or why you were asking some subpart of the question, they can no longer follow this strategy."  
  > -- `research__214_buck_shlegeris_on_controlling_ai_that_wants_to_57e8f430` (2025-04-04; solo author)

**D3 – accept/reject**
- Check whether a model can be trained to tell synthetic from real; if it can, reject the realism. 
  > "construct a dataset of innocuous off-policy actions (e.g. ask one of the people who is in charge of generating synthetic attacks to generate some synthetic innocuous actions that they think look like actions the policy would take in the course of a normal trajectory)"  
  > -- `research__how_to_prevent_collusion_when_using_untrusted_mode_07a37f70` (2024-09-25; solo author) 
  > "if a scheming model is trained on model-generated inputs, especially adversarially generated ones, it might learn to distinguish between real inputs and model-generated ones, or learn a heuristic of generally being more conservative in situations where inputs are model-generated."  
  > -- `research__behavioral_red_teaming_is_unlikely_to_produce_clea_ff0a83d6` (2024-10-10; solo author)
- Require a large Bayes factor, not a merely reasonable-looking test. 
  > "My basic concern with BRT as a schemer risk mitigation strategy is that, though I think it might get you a Bayes factor of 2, it seems really hard for it to get you a Bayes factor of 10."  
  > -- `research__behavioral_red_teaming_is_unlikely_to_produce_clea_ff0a83d6` (2024-10-10; solo author) 
  > "you start out with like a one is to a million prior on any particular attack that you see that you are being honeypotted. And so you have to somehow get a one-in-a-million likelihood ratio update towards this being real."  
  > -- `research__214_buck_shlegeris_on_controlling_ai_that_wants_to_57e8f430` (2025-04-04; solo author)
- Rule out the "infeasible" null before reading low rates. 
  > "If side tasks are intrinsically hard, low sabotage rates in § 5.2 could just mean the attacker couldn’t do the task, not that the monitor caught it. We need to rule this out."  
  > -- `research__linuxarena_a_control_setting_for_ai_agentsin_live__48e03bb2` (2026-04-16; middle author)
- Interpret negative results only conditional on proxy validity and elicitation. 
  > "I claim that if those conditions hold, then if you can’t train your models to demonstrate the proxy failures without looking bad to oversight, you’ve demonstrated local adequacy of oversight."  
  > -- `research__meta_level_adversarial_evaluation_of_oversight_tec_effed282` (2023-07-26; first author)

**D4 – pursue/abandon**
- Red-team throughout deployment instead of relying on pre-deployment synthetic inputs. 
  > "I propose red-teaming throughout deployment, which mitigates the difficulty of synthesizing inputs, and I note that untrusted monitors can’t follow rare failure strategies."  
  > -- `research__behavioral_red_teaming_is_unlikely_to_produce_clea_ff0a83d6` (2024-10-10; solo author) 
  > "the policy has a conceptually easy strategy to counter synthetic input tests: it can choose a low probability of attacking on any particular input, such that it's very hard for you to find an input where it attacks"  
  > -- `research__how_to_prevent_collusion_when_using_untrusted_mode_07a37f70` (2024-09-25; solo author)
- Invest early in setting construction. 
  > "When we were writing the first paper in the APPS setting, I did not appreciate how much harder it would be to construct settings for subsequent projects. And I really messed up by not putting more emphasis on this at the start of the Ctrl-Z project."  
  > -- `research__why_it_s_hard_to_make_settings_for_high_stakes_con_ff38a639` (2025-07-18; solo author)
- Pursue conservative assumptions for about half of the work. 
  > "I currently think that about half of the AI control research should make these conservative assumptions. But I’m less enthusiastic about these assumptions than I was a year ago."  
  > -- `research__thoughts_on_the_conservative_assumptions_in_ai_con_79585e0f` (2025-01-17; solo author)

**D5 – surprising results**
- Hard adversarial search finding bad behaviour is not evidence of scheming. 
  > "if you apply these techniques hard enough, you'll probably find inputs that cause the AI to behave badly regardless of whether the model is a schemer or not, because models aren't very adversarially robust."  
  > -- `research__behavioral_red_teaming_is_unlikely_to_produce_clea_ff0a83d6` (2024-10-10; solo author)
- Enumerate competing explanations and judge by direct experience. 
  > "It’s really felt like fundamental weaknesses of the models, rather than scaffold limitations, are the main reason that they haven’t been more useful to us."  
  > -- `research__where_is_all_the_ai_safety_research_uplift_304e87c9` (2026-11-09; solo author) 
  > "this speedup was partially due to the project being pretty amenable to massive agent use (because it involved reading lots of stuff) and partially due to Ryan being experienced with insane agent workflows."  
  > -- `research__where_is_all_the_ai_safety_research_uplift_304e87c9` (2026-11-09; solo author)

**D6 – what to claim**
- Claim relative improvements rather than absolute scores. 
  > "The blue team’s absolute performance is highly sensitive to this parameter, but the relative performance between our protocols is fairly insensitive to it. Hence, we think the relative improvements of our protocols are a more important result than the absolute scores."  
  > -- `research__ctrl_z_controlling_ai_agents_via_resampling_1cbfd6cb` (2025-04-14; last author)
- Scope claims to the historical system tested. 
  > "Our findings describe the historical system we assessed on and before July 21st, rather than the expanded system’s current coverage, which this exercise did not establish."  
  > -- `research__red_teaming_openai_s_internal_agent_monitoring_sys_73bb3ad9` (2026-10-22; solo author)
- Be conservative about model capabilities. 
  > "I normally recommend being conservative about whether they can coordinate on a code, so I normally recommend assuming that the AIs did set up a code in advance."  
  > -- `research__214_buck_shlegeris_on_controlling_ai_that_wants_to_57e8f430` (2025-04-04; solo author) 
  > "We don’t therefore say “safety is zero, because we’ve demonstrated that there are actions that the AI could output that would be catastrophic”. Instead, we measure the proportion of the time that the scaffold’s code gets past all the safety measures"  
  > -- `research__thoughts_on_the_conservative_assumptions_in_ai_con_79585e0f` (2025-01-17; solo author)

**Distrusts**
- Synthetic inputs with hidden tells. 
  > "I don’t expect it to be impossible to generate synthetic inputs like this, but it might be a huge amount of effort, and it might be really hard to be sure that none of the stuff you faked has any tells"  
  > -- `research__behavioral_red_teaming_is_unlikely_to_produce_clea_ff0a83d6` (2024-10-10; solo author) 
  > "our environments use synthetic placeholder data rather than real production data. A sufficiently capable model might notice this and infer that it is operating in an evaluation, though we have no evidence this is currently happening."  
  > -- `research__linuxarena_a_control_setting_for_ai_agentsin_live__48e03bb2` (2026-04-16; middle author)
- Models generating their own test inputs. 
  > "if you’re asking the model itself to generate the synthetic inputs, it’s very plausible it would purposefully generate inputs with tells in them. So you might be restricted to using other, and thus possibly weaker models."  
  > -- `research__behavioral_red_teaming_is_unlikely_to_produce_clea_ff0a83d6` (2024-10-10; solo author) 
  > "some of the attack strategies that Ryan Greenblatt came up with included "use a 'while loop' somewhere where a 'for loop' would have been more idiomatic as the signal that this is a real attack.""  
  > -- `research__214_buck_shlegeris_on_controlling_ai_that_wants_to_57e8f430` (2025-04-04; solo author)
- Attacks depending only superficially on context. 
  > "The resulting attacks depend only superficially on the context - GPT-4o mini is provided with a human-written attack template, and surrounds the provided malicious commands with distracting innocuous code."  
  > -- `research__ctrl_z_controlling_ai_agents_via_resampling_1cbfd6cb` (2025-04-14; last author)
- Magically informed attack policies. 
  > "The attack policy is magically informed of the side task for each trajectory, but the protocol isn’t. This is fundamentally unrealistic."  
  > -- `research__why_it_s_hard_to_make_settings_for_high_stakes_con_ff38a639` (2025-07-18; solo author)
- Sandwiching and clean evals as clearance. 
  > "a misaligned model might be able to sabotage a sandwiching evaluations by purposefully giving good answers in domains where it knows that its developers have access to held out information, and answer much worse in cases where it knows we don't have access to the held out information."  
  > -- `research__meta_level_adversarial_evaluation_of_oversight_tec_effed282` (2023-07-26; first author) 
  > "Both of these strategies (or their combination) seem simple and easy enough that it’s plausible that a schemer could both think of them and execute on them successfully, and would lead the schemer to look about as innocent as a non-scheming model."  
  > -- `research__behavioral_red_teaming_is_unlikely_to_produce_clea_ff0a83d6` (2024-10-10; solo author)
- Developer claims left unverified. 
  > "OpenAI has stated that all of the vulnerabilities we identified that impact their production safeguards stack have been patched. OpenAI has also described significant subsequent changes to the intended coverage of its monitoring system. We have not evaluated these claims."  
  > -- `research__red_teaming_openai_s_internal_agent_monitoring_sys_73bb3ad9` (2026-10-22; solo author)
